messages:
Michael G: Hey all — first week! Finished MDM enrollment on my new M1 MacBook Air but running into a weird one: when I try to launch an old Intel-only app it flickers a prompt to install Rosetta and then nothing happens. Docker Desktop also shows 'admin approval required' for a system extension and the prompt disappears. Anyone seen Jamf block Rosetta/admin prompts? Do I need a temporary admin?

Alex (IT): welcome @Michael G :wave: Jamf can definitely suppress interactive installers. Quick checks: which macOS build are you on, and can you paste the exact error when you try the Rosetta install? We can push Rosetta via MDM or give you a short-lived admin.

Michael G: macOS 13.5.1. When I try the suggested command I get a permissions error. Output: ```sudo softwareupdate --install-rosetta --agree-to-license
Password:
installer: Package name is "Rosetta 2"
installer: authentication required
installer: Authorization failed (1)```

Alex (IT): thanks. That looks like Jamf is preventing interactive authorization. Can you run this to list enrollment profiles and paste results? ```sudo profiles show -type enrollment || sudo profiles -P``` If that returns a managed profile we can target a push.

Michael G: pasted output: ```Profiles: 1 enrollment profile: com.jamf.management, status: managed by Jamf Pro```

Alex (IT): yep — Jamf. Two easy options: 1) I can push the Rosetta package via Jamf (no interaction needed) — I need the device ID which you can get with `sudo jamf getComputerName` or the hardware UUID from About This Mac -> System Report -> Hardware -> Hardware UUID. 2) We can create a temp local admin for you (we'll delete it after). Which do you prefer?

Priya (People Ops): tagging IT flow — if you need admin for more than 2 hours please file an onboarding IT ticket at it-help@redwood.com so we can track. For quick fixes IT usually does a Jamf push.

Michael G: thanks. I can grab the hardware UUID now. One more question: will pushing Rosetta affect my FileVault / startup behavior? I have FileVault enabled by default.

Alex (IT): pushing Rosetta via Jamf is safe with FileVault enabled — it installs as a system update. For the Docker system extension approval, Jamf can also push the Approved Kernel Extension/Driver payload or set the kext allowlist. If Docker still asks, reboot after the push and try again.

Sam (Eng): FYI, for a lot of CLI tools you can avoid Rosetta by installing ARM-native Homebrew packages (if available). But for closed-source Intel apps Rosetta is required.

Alex (IT): Michael, if you paste the hardware UUID here I'll schedule the Jamf policy to push Rosetta and the Docker kext allowlist. Should be a 5–10 minute rollout, then reboot.

Michael G: UUID: 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000 (pasted). Appreciate it.

Jamf Bot: Policy "Install Rosetta 2" queued for device 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000. Estimated completion: ~3 minutes.

Alex (IT): pushed the Docker allowlist as well. When the policy completes, please restart and try launching Docker and the Intel app.

Michael G: rebooted — Rosetta installer ran silently on boot and the app launches now. Docker started without prompts. Thanks Alex and team :raised_hands:

Priya (People Ops): glad that worked — welcome to Redwood! If you need any other permissions shout here or open a ticket.

Michael G: all good, closing this one. :thumbsup:
